issue_context.title: Cannot filter aliased column after `join` (in lazy mode)
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
lf = polars.LazyFrame({"col1": [True, False, True, False], "col2": range(4), "col3": range(10,14)})
lf_other = polars.LazyFrame({"col4": [0, 11, 2, 13], "col5": range(20, 24)})

lf = lf.with_columns(
    polars.when(polars.col("col1") == True)
    .then(polars.col("col2"))
    .otherwise(polars.col("col3"))
    .alias("new_col"))

# filtering by aliased column works
print(lf.filter(polars.col("new_col") < 12).collect())
# ┌───────┬──────┬──────┬─────────┐
# │ col1  ┆ col2 ┆ col3 ┆ new_col │
# │ ---   ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---     │
# │ bool  ┆ i64  ┆ i64  ┆ i64     │
# ╞═══════╪══════╪══════╪═════════╡
# │ true  ┆ 0    ┆ 10   ┆ 0       │
# │ false ┆ 1    ┆ 11   ┆ 11      │
# │ true  ┆ 2    ┆ 12   ┆ 2       │
# └───────┴──────┴──────┴─────────┘

lf = lf.join(lf_other, left_on="new_col", right_on="col4", how="left")
df = lf.collect()
print(df)
# ┌───────┬──────┬──────┬─────────┬──────┐
# │ col1  ┆ col2 ┆ col3 ┆ new_col ┆ col5 │
# │ ---   ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---     ┆ ---  │
# │ bool  ┆ i64  ┆ i64  ┆ i64     ┆ i64  │
# ╞═══════╪══════╪══════╪═════════╪══════╡
# │ true  ┆ 0    ┆ 10   ┆ 0       ┆ 20   │
# │ false ┆ 1    ┆ 11   ┆ 11      ┆ 21   │
# │ true  ┆ 2    ┆ 12   ┆ 2       ┆ 22   │
# │ false ┆ 3    ┆ 13   ┆ 13      ┆ 23   │
# └───────┴──────┴──────┴─────────┴──────┘

# after `join`, filtering by original column name works
lf_selection = lf.select(["col5", "col2", "col3"])
lf_selection_filtered = lf_selection.filter(polars.col("col5") < 23)
lf_selection.collect()
lf_selection_filtered.collect()

# after `join`, selecting by aliased column name works
lf_selection_with_aliased_col = lf.select(["new_col", "col2", "col3"])
print(lf_selection_with_aliased_col.collect())  # works even with `streaming=True`
# ┌─────────┬──────┬──────┐
# │ new_col ┆ col2 ┆ col3 │
# │ ---     ┆ ---  ┆ ---  │
# │ i64     ┆ i64  ┆ i64  │
# ╞═════════╪══════╪══════╡
# │ 0       ┆ 0    ┆ 10   │
# │ 11      ┆ 1    ┆ 11   │
# │ 2       ┆ 2    ┆ 12   │
# │ 13      ┆ 3    ┆ 13   │
# └─────────┴──────┴──────┘

print("Eager mode seems to work nicely: ", df.select(["new_col", "col2", "col3"]).filter(polars.col("new_col") < 12))

# exception: after `join`, filtering by aliased column name stops working
lf_selection_with_aliased_col_and_filter = lf_selection_with_aliased_col.filter(polars.col("new_col") < 12)
lf_selection_with_aliased_col_and_filter.collect()  # `ColumnNotFoundError: new_col`
```

---> 49 lf_selection_with_aliased_col_and_filter.collect()  # `ColumnNotFoundError: new_col`

File ~/mambaforge-pypy3/envs/quantlab/lib/python3.10/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/frame.py:1706, in LazyFrame.collect(self, type_coercion, predicate_pushdown, projection_pushdown, simplify_expression, slice_pushdown, comm_subplan_elim, comm_subexpr_elim, no_optimization, streaming, _eager)
   1693     comm_subplan_elim = False

   1696     type_coercion,

ColumnNotFoundError: new_col

### Issue description

It looks like after a join (in lazy mode), we cannot filter by column that we created before using `.with_columns` and `.alias` anymore.

### Expected behavior

Would expect the same behavior of `.filter` as before the `.join` operation.

comments:
Seems to be `predicate_pushdown` related.

```python
>>> lf_selection_with_aliased_col_and_filter.collect(predicate_pushdown=False)
shape: (3, 3)
┌─────────┬──────┬──────┐
│ new_col ┆ col2 ┆ col3 │
│ ---     ┆ ---  ┆ ---  │
│ i64     ┆ i64  ┆ i64  │
╞═════════╪══════╪══════╡
│ 0       ┆ 0    ┆ 10   │
│ 11      ┆ 1    ┆ 11   │
│ 2       ┆ 2    ┆ 12   │
└─────────┴──────┴──────┘
```

Minimal repro:

```python
lf = pl.LazyFrame({"col3": range(10,14)})
lf_other = pl.LazyFrame({"col4": [0, 11, 2, 13]})

lf = lf.with_columns(pl.col("col3").alias("new_col"))
lf = lf.join(lf_other, left_on="new_col", right_on="col4", how="left")
lf = lf.filter(pl.col("new_col") < 12)
lf.collect()  
```
